task: Fix the incorrect search results after the inverted index tokenizer was changed.

candidate_memories.content: Search results for hyphenated terms now return zero results after the tokenizer was changed to split on hyphens.
The search analyzer must use the custom_compound tokenizer that preserves hyphenated terms as single tokens.
The tokenizer was changed from custom_compound to standard in the last index rebuild without testing hyphenated queries.
When changing search analyzers, run a regression test with the full query log before rebuilding the index.
Non-hyphenated search queries return correct results; only hyphenated product names and brand names are affected.
The search index was rebuilt on April 12 as part of the quarterly index maintenance.
Session 6 note: the search team added boosting for exact phrase matches.
Old lesson: the standard tokenizer was used before custom tokenizers were introduced for multi-language support.
Elasticsearch is used for full-text search; the version is 8.12.
Session 11 note: synonym support was added for common brand name abbreviations.
Old search guide: the custom_compound tokenizer was added to handle German compound words.
Search analyzer changes must be validated with production query samples before a full index rebuild.
Session 4 note: the search ranking model was updated with a new TF-IDF weighting.
The search index has 8.5 million documents and rebuilds take approximately 4 hours.
A search accuracy report in session 9 showed 94% relevance for non-hyphenated queries.
Faceted filters are implemented as Elasticsearch aggregations, not as index-level filters.
When choosing tokenizers, test with real production queries that include edge cases like hyphens and numbers.
Session 7 note: the autocomplete feature was extended to support partial word matching.
Old index guide: the index rebuild was triggered manually by the search team before it was automated.
Search queries go through the API gateway with a 2-second timeout before falling back to the database.
